To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the proposed multi-dimensional dynamic time warping algorithm is a good alternative to the ordinary one-dimensional algorithm, (ii) the proposed algorithm can be applied to both raw feature values and derivatives of the feature values and (iii) the algorithm is robust against noise and can be used to classify gestures.
(1) DTW is a good method for gesture recognition, (2) DTW on derivatives is better than DTW on values and (3) using all dimensions in DTW improves performance.
(1) MD-DTW performed better than 1D-DTW, (2) DTW on derivatives performed better than DTW on values, and (3) DTW on the derivative of a single dimension gave the best results
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of algorithms that are able to handle multi-dimensionality of the data and to perform classification of gestures.
the use of multi-dimensional Dynamic Time Warping in a gesture classification task.
the problem of gesture recognition in a noisy environment.

MD-DTW is a useful algorithm for gesture recognition.

the use of multiple features in DTW is a promising method for gesture recognition, especially under noisy conditions.

the best results were obtained by using the MD-DTW on feature derivatives.
the proposed MD-DTW is a good method for gesture classification and that the use of derivatives instead of feature value is beneficial.

using all dimensions in a DTW algorithm gives better classification accuracy than using only one dimension.
